App at a glance: August 24-29

Alayna Day, Associate Arts & Culture Editor
August 24, 2026
Liz Townsend

Monday, Aug. 24

Blue Bag Drive

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:16
Instaread

Pick up a reusable recycling bag from 12-2 p.m. on Sanford Mall and learn about reducing waste on campus and how you can recycle in your dorm with App State’s Sustainability and Energy Management. 

 

Tuesday, Aug. 25

Health, Wellness and Safety Fest

Wellness and Prevention Services and Mountaineer Recovery Community are holding the Health, Wellness and Safety Fest from 1-4 p.m. on Sanford Mall. Join in on a campuswide scavenger hunt, yard games, free giveaways and learn about the many services available to students at App State. 

 

Wednesday, Aug. 26

Guided Tour of the Historic Appalachian Theatre

Explore the history of Boone staple The Appalachian Theatre of the High Country from 3-4 p.m. and be led through the refreshed 1938 Art Deco building before viewing a documentary detailing the theatre’s life from past to present.

 

Thursday, Aug. 27 

The Weekly Refresh

Students are invited to The Weekly Refresh to participate in a variety of activities to de-stress, reset and meet new people. Join App State’s Counseling and Psychological Services and Mental Health Ambassadors in the Grandfather Mountain Ballroom in Plemmons Student Union from 12-2 p.m.

 

Friday, Aug. 28

Game On!

Appalachian Campus Dining welcomes students to a game night in the Jimmy Smith Lounge of Rivers Street Café located in Central Dining Hall. Bring friends and join in on a variety of board games and video games from 6-9 p.m.

 

Summer Concerts at the Jones House 

Catch the last Jones House summer concert of the 2026 season at 5:30 p.m. With performances from Meris Gantt & Devin Lacey and Gary McCullough & South on Something, join the audience for a night of music and community. 

 

Saturday, Aug. 29

Annual Fairy Day in the Gardens

Daniel Boone Native Gardens is hosting its annual Fairy Day full of music, crafts, vendors and whimsical fun from 1-5 p.m. The price for adults is $5, and all admission proceeds go to supporting the gardens and keeping native plants in Boone. 

 

Artist-in-Residence D. Zisl Slepovitch

Zisl Slepovitch will serve a 3-day residency presented by App State’s Center for Judaic, Holocaust and Peace Studies, App State’s Hayes School of Music and the Temple of the High Country, bringing his acclaimed music and scholarship with him. Saturday at 4 p.m., Slepovitch will perform “Songs from Testimonies: Music from the Fortunoff Video Archive for Holocaust Testimonies” in the Broyhill Music Center, exploring testimonies from the Holocaust, Yiddish music and cultural heritage.
